forestall

/for-STAWL/ - rhymes with tall · verb

Hear It

What It Means

Forestall means to prevent something by acting ahead of time.

Knowing the twins would fight over the last slice, their mother forestalled the argument by cutting it in two before dinner.

Example

The festival's planners forestalled the annual parking chaos by chartering shuttle buses a month in advance and selling lot passes with every ticket.

Any barrier can prevent; forestall specifically means getting ahead of the problem. The timing is the point — you see what is coming and act early enough that it never gets started at all.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

preempt: To preempt is to act first so that another's move never happens or no longer matters — it needs a rival plan to beat. To forestall needs no rival: you see any kind of trouble coming and act early enough that it never starts.

preclude: To preclude is to shut a possibility off in advance — the rule, the design, or the circumstance makes the thing impossible, no foresight story required. To forestall is personal and tactical: someone reads what is coming and moves early to stop it.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

invite: to make something more likely to happen

trigger: to set something off directly

Where it sits · how early you act against trouble — contain → avert → forestall

contain vs. forestall: Containing a problem is weaker than forestalling it — the trouble has already begun, and you are only limiting its spread.

avert vs. forestall: Averting is a step short of forestalling — a disaster can be averted at the last instant, while forestalling means you moved long before the danger was even close.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — fore-

Prefix — fore-: before, in front (Old English)

Root — stall

Root — stall: a fixed place, position, or stand (Old English steall)

Put it together

Put it together: Fore- (before) + stall (a fixed place or stand) = to take the position first. A medieval forestaller waylaid goods on the road and bought them up before they ever reached the market stalls; the word kept the trick — get there ahead of events, and they never happen.

Use the root in a new word: install

Use the root in a new word: install: The technicians install the dishwasher on Tuesday, setting it into its place beneath the counter.

Word Choice

formal

Forestall is the strategist's word: it praises foresight, not reflexes. Use 'prevent' when timing doesn't matter and 'avert' for the last-second save; reach for forestall when someone read the future and moved early. Unlike its unit-mates quell and neutralize, which deal with trouble already alive, forestall wins by making sure the trouble is never born.
